title: Lesson 3 Quiz: Financial Risk and Financial Inclusion
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not reviewed or approved by a human (admin); do not give to students.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: You get a text that claims to be from your bank. It says your account will be closed within an hour unless you pay a $200 fee with gift cards. Which response fits the warning signs described in this lesson?

choices.text: Pay quickly, since closing the account would cost you more
Reply to the text and ask the sender to prove who they are
Pay half now and promise the rest after checking your balance
Stop, and contact the bank using a number you already trust

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Tom put his savings into a 3-year certificate of deposit. Six months later his car breaks down, and getting the money out early means paying a penalty. Which type of risk is this?

Hypothetical example: Nina splits $1,200 equally among three investments. Over the period, the first gains 8%, the second gains 2%, and the third loses 20%. How much is her total worth at the end, in dollars? (Enter a number only.)

Hypothetical example: An investor holds small amounts of shares in 300 different companies across many industries. A recession then lowers profits at most companies. What is the most likely effect on the portfolio?

choices.text: It is protected, because 300 companies offset one another's losses
It falls by more than one company would, because losses add up
It probably loses value, because a market-wide shock is hard to diversify
It is unaffected, because recessions mainly hurt single companies

questions.prompt: Which policy is the clearest example of the financial inclusion called for in SDG target 8.10?

choices.text: Raising the minimum balance for opening a savings account
Helping local institutions offer low-cost accounts and insurance to all
Closing rural bank branches to lower the costs of urban banking
Offering high-interest loans with fees that are not disclosed
